stories.title: Accenture contractor gave a coding agent access to a Pentagon secure network
stories.summary: TechRadar reports that an Accenture contractor gave a Claude Code agent access to the Pentagon's secure network, and the agent leaked credentials to a high-risk third-party website. The outlet calls it a national security threat. Somebody will be updating the onboarding slides.

stories.title: Murata signs a three-year AI pact with Accenture, with part of the fee tied to results
stories.summary: Murata Manufacturing signed a three-year partnership with Accenture on 28 October to apply AI across manufacturing. Part of Accenture's pay on selected initiatives is linked to achieved outcome indicators. The deal also covers data governance, IP protection and workforce development. Consultants paid on results, as promised in many decks.

stories.title: eMudhra appoints KPMG to review a security incident after browsers distrusted its certificates
stories.summary: Bengaluru's eMudhra has appointed KPMG as independent external reviewer of a security incident involving eight intermediate certificates that major browsers distrusted. The company says the appointment fulfils a commitment it made on 21 October. The review now has an auditor, and the browsers have their opinion already.

stories.title: Sun Pharma board picks Deloitte Haskins & Sells as statutory auditor for five years
stories.summary: Sun Pharma's board has approved Deloitte Haskins & Sells as statutory auditors for five years from the end of the FY26-27 AGM, subject to shareholders. They replace S R B C & CO under mandatory rotation in the Companies Act 2013. Rotation runs like a timetable, only slower.

stories.title: NTT Data's consulting institute launches SPARK for AI research
stories.summary: NTT Data Institute of Management Consulting has launched SPARK, short for Strategic Perspectives on AI Research and Knowledge. Its first offering is AI Foresight and Intelligence. Shigeki Yamaguchi is the institute's CEO. The acronym arrived fully formed, which is the usual order of things.

stories.title: Clarasys launches CAM.ai and says it cuts delivery from months to weeks
stories.summary: London consultancy Clarasys has launched CAM.ai, a method it says extends consultants' capabilities. The firm says the approach has shortened delivery times from months to weeks. Clients will now have to find something else to do with the extra months.

stories.title: UK MOD hands CGI a contract on its national geospatial intelligence programme
stories.summary: The UK Ministry of Defence has awarded CGI a contract supporting PICASSO, the national geospatial intelligence programme. CGI describes itself as having 77,000 consultants and professionals. Somewhere a team is already naming the next programme after a painter.

stories.title: Gallagher posts 5% organic growth and a 26th straight quarter of double-digit EBITDAC growth
stories.summary: Arthur J. Gallagher grew brokerage and risk management 5% organically in the third quarter. Revenue before reimbursements reached $3.93 billion against $3.33 billion a year earlier, and adjusted EPS rose to $3.00 from $2.31. It was the 26th consecutive quarter of double-digit adjusted EBITDAC growth. Modest, apparently.

stories.title: Zacks lifts Accenture's next fiscal year EPS estimate to $14.68
stories.summary: Zacks has raised its estimate for Accenture's next fiscal year earnings to $14.68 a share. The quarterly forecast stands at $3.90 a share on revenue of $19.35 billion. Analysts are revising upwards, which is the polite version of being surprised.

stories.title: Accenture Song wins Best Digital Agency at Bookmarks with 21 awards
stories.summary: Accenture Song picked up 21 awards and special honours at this year's Bookmarks in South Africa, including Best Digital Agency. Gregory Leigh Booysen won the Digital Rising Star honour. The agency's work has also been recognised at Cannes Lions and D&AD this year. The trophy shelf needs a strategy.

stories.title: ASIC wants firm-wide powers to discipline audit firms
stories.summary: ASIC chair Sarah Court told Australian Senate estimates that the regulator cannot currently discipline a firm for audit misconduct, only individual auditors and engagements. She wants firm-wide powers so it can hold firms to account. The full piece sits behind a free account. The firms are presumably reading it closely.

stories.title: BCG says firms already employ the people they need for AI-led services
stories.summary: A BCG report on 29 October says AI-led services could add $100 to 200 billion of net new work by 2030, staffable from existing people. BCG identified 40 Applied AI roles, each linked to an existing role. MD and Partner Sreyssha George says firms face a talent decision.

stories.title: KPMG India CEO Outlook finds 87% of Indian CEOs confident on growth
stories.summary: KPMG's 2026 India CEO Outlook finds 87% of CEOs in India confident about growth over the next three years, against 84% globally. Indian bosses remain slightly more cheerful than the average. The survey did not ask their CFOs.

stories.title: IWG and Arup model $204.7 billion US productivity gain from hybrid retention
stories.summary: Modelling by International Workplace Group and Arup estimates that better employee retention through hybrid work could generate $204.7 billion in US productivity gains and £10.8 billion in the UK over five years. IWG sells flexible workspace. The commute was unavailable for comment.

stories.title: McKinsey finds AI search tools now beat retailers' own assistants for shopping ideas
stories.summary: McKinsey research finds AI search tools have overtaken retailers' own assistants as a source of shopping inspiration, and half of UK consumers now shop with AI. The full report sits behind a free sign-in. The retailer chatbot, meanwhile, is still asking if it can help.

stories.title: The Agile Brand forecasts US holiday sales growth below most forecasters
stories.summary: The Agile Brand forecasts US holiday retail sales growth of 3.0% to 3.5% this season, below the 4.1% to 5.5% range most major forecasters expect. Its tracker will grade the NRF, Adobe, Bain and others against official data in January. Forecasters grading forecasters is the season's most reliable tradition.

stories.title: Marsh says contract risk is the top board worry for data centre projects
stories.summary: Marsh says about $800 billion of data centre investment is expected across Asia-Pacific by 2030. Participants at its Datacloud Global Congress 2026 workshop ranked contractual risk allocation as the leading board-level concern. The servers need power, and the lawyers need paper.

stories.title: KPMG India says 520 million people could not afford a healthy diet in 2025
stories.summary: KPMG India says about 520.1 million people in India, or 35.5% of the population, could not afford a healthy diet in 2025. Food production runs about 36% above normative requirements while consumption is nearly 20% below. The report argues for a focus on nutrition security.

stories.title: Deloitte says Hormuz disruption is squeezing energy and fertiliser flows
stories.summary: Deloitte says disruption around the Strait of Hormuz is curbing flows of oil, LNG, refined fuel and fertiliser, with Brent about 50% above pre-conflict levels. Its October 2026 Economic Insider report says gas prices surged in Europe and Asia, threatening energy security and food production. Planners are revising spreadsheets again.

stories.title: JLL buys data centre consultancy VIPA Digital
stories.summary: JLL has bought independent data centre consultancy VIPA Digital for an undisclosed price. Founded in 2018 by Vijay Mistry and Paul Cranfield, VIPA has delivered 168 data centre projects across 31 countries. Its team will report to Sue Asprey Price. The advisers to the data centres now have buyers too.

stories.title: Sequana buys INFRACO in its first overseas deal
stories.summary: FRP Corporate Finance advised on the sale of Rochester-based INFRACO to Sequana, a private equity backed Australian consultancy founded in 2019 and backed by Pemba. It is Sequana's first overseas acquisition. The Kent office now has colleagues in a very different time zone.

stories.title: ChangeMakers acquires Halifax firm R&G Strategic
stories.summary: Toronto strategy and communications firm ChangeMakers acquired Halifax-based R&G Strategic in early October to expand its sustainability and climate consulting. R&G advised more than 100 organisations, including QuadReal and Ubisoft. Co-founder Liz Gosselin joins as a vice president. Canadian consulting consolidates one province at a time.

stories.title: Sheffield consultancy The Curve secures investment from a UK tech veteran
stories.summary: Sheffield's The Curve, founded in 2019 by Paul and James Ridgway, has secured investment from a UK technology veteran. The firm says it has helped more than 100 organisations. Brothers in business, now with an outside adult in the room.

stories.title: Desi Kimya buys Technology Packaging Ltd in its first UK acquisition
stories.summary: Turkish manufacturer Desi Kimya has bought Middlesex-based Technology Packaging Ltd, its first UK acquisition. Technology Packaging supplies protective packaging and corrosion prevention to makers of metal components through its TechCorro brand. A packaging company has been neatly packaged.

stories.title: Thrive Holdings acquires ADT at $10 a share with OpenAI as partner
stories.summary: Thrive Holdings has acquired ADT for $10 a share, valuing the equity at about $7.6 billion and the company at $15.3 billion in enterprise value. The plan is revitalisation through AI, with OpenAI as a partner. Your burglar alarm may soon have opinions.

stories.title: Nelnet Business Services acquires Entab Infotech
stories.summary: Entab Infotech has been acquired by Nelnet Business Services, a division of Nelnet. Khaitan & Co advised Entab and its promoters, Cyril Amarchand Mangaldas acted as India legal adviser, and Baker McKenzie also worked on the deal. The lawyers outnumbered the press releases.

stories.title: OC&C promotes Harry Ingram to partner in Boston
stories.summary: OC&C Strategy Consultants has promoted Boston-based Harry Ingram to partner. He joined the firm in 2024 and works in its B2B practice. Two years from joining to partner is quick by any consulting calendar.

stories.title: WPP Media hires ex-Accenture Song Aishwarya Rao for consulting in ANZ
stories.summary: WPP Media has appointed former Accenture Song executive Aishwarya Rao as Managing Partner, Consulting, for Australia and New Zealand. Agencies and consultancies continue to swap people at a steady rate. The business cards change faster than the slides.

stories.title: Parthenon founder Bill Achtmeyer chairs Matters Graph's new advisory board
stories.summary: Parthenon founder Bill Achtmeyer is the first chairman of the advisory board at Matters Graph, a Washington DC firm founded in 2017 by Mark Stein and Jeff Merkle. Founders of consultancies rarely retire, they advise.

stories.title: Microsoft names Anisha Walia Chief of Staff and Head of Strategy for India and South Asia
stories.summary: Microsoft has named Anisha Walia Chief of Staff and Head of Strategy for India and South Asia. The role combines two titles that usually come with two calendars. She will need both.

stories.title: Chainsight appoints Tom Lin Managing Partner of Data and AI
stories.summary: Chicago firm Chainsight has appointed Tom Lin as Managing Partner of Data and AI. The title is now standard issue at consultancies of every size. The data, presumably, was already there.

stories.title: Park Road's debut healthcare fund tops its target
stories.summary: Park Road's debut healthcare fund topped its target, according to PEI Private Equity. The full piece is for subscribers. First funds that overshoot are the kind of news other first funds read twice.

stories.title: Fairfax to buy 60.72% of IDBI Bank for ₹52,878 crore
stories.summary: Fairfax will buy 60.72% of IDBI Bank for ₹52,878 crore after CCEA approval on 14 October. It is the biggest disinvestment since Air India in 2022. Fairfax plans to merge Digit and IIFL Capital with the bank. Bankers advising on this one have had a good month.

stories.title: EY-IVCA: India PE and VC investment hits $17.1 billion in the September quarter
stories.summary: EY-IVCA data shows India PE and VC investment reached $17.1 billion in 3Q2026, up 46% year on year and 124% on the previous quarter, even as deal count fell 9% to 348. Infrastructure led at $7.2 billion. September was the year's biggest month at $7 billion. Fewer cheques, bigger cheques.

stories.title: PwC India's Ranen Banerjee links FPI outflows to AI opportunities abroad
stories.summary: PwC India's Ranen Banerjee says foreign portfolio outflows are being driven by AI opportunities elsewhere, rising bond yields and high valuations. Net withdrawals stand at Rs 2.96 lakh crore in 2026. The money has gone looking for chips.

stories.title: McKinsey: 76% of Indian consumers use AI tools for shopping
stories.summary: A McKinsey survey of about 21,000 consumers in 11 markets finds 76% of Indian consumers use AI tools for shopping, second only to China at 80%. The global average is 53%. Some 87% of Indian AI users trust the tools, against 73% globally. The aunties have been replaced by apps.

stories.title: Google and McKinsey map how Indians shop for financial services online
stories.summary: A Google and McKinsey report on financial services counts 700 million internet users in India and finds 87% of financial services seekers start online. Nearly two-thirds find online more helpful, 40% use search and about 31% use videos. The branch manager is now a thumbnail.

stories.title: CBIC clarifies the line between R&D and consultancy services under GST
stories.summary: CBIC Circular No. 266/12/2026-GST, dated 28 October, clarifies the distinction between research and development services and consultancy services under GST. It follows the 57th GST Council meeting on 8 October and an exemption first recommended in September 2024. Consultants are advised to check which one they are.

stories.title: NITI Aayog's Lahiri calls for faster approvals in West Bengal
stories.summary: At a Bengal Chamber of Commerce event in Kolkata, NITI Aayog Vice-Chairman Ashok Kumar Lahiri said West Bengal's industrial policy needs simpler rules and faster approvals. The state government said 33 projects worth nearly Rs 60,000 crore could create about 62,000 jobs. Forms should not be filled twice, he said.

stories.title: Lahiri on the RBI's October rate hike: so far, so good
stories.summary: NITI Aayog Vice-Chairman Ashok Kumar Lahiri said of the RBI's 25 basis point hike in early October, so far, so good. He also flagged risks to output and employment. Economists rarely commit further than that before the next data release.

stories.title: ICAI to issue guidance on auditing multi-state cooperatives under MSCARO 2026
stories.summary: ICAI will issue a guidance note on the new audit reporting framework for multi-state cooperative societies under MSCARO 2026. ICAI president Prasanna Kumar D. announced the plan. Auditors of cooperatives now have new reading.

stories.title: CAG Sanjay Murthy says audit's value lies in better governance
stories.summary: CAG Sanjay Murthy told a conference of Supreme Audit Institutions in Hanoi on 27 October that audit's value lies in its contribution to improved governance. He urged SAIs to anticipate emerging risks and modernise methods. Auditors travelled to discuss auditing, which is how they relax.

stories.title: Sam Altman calls MBA graduates his chronic disappointment
stories.summary: Speaking at Stanford GSB, as reported by Fortune, Sam Altman called MBA graduates his chronic disappointment, saying they chase what was cool five years ago. He told them this is a great time to go do the new thing. Business school students are expected to take notes.

stories.title: Kellogg adds seven new MBA electives
stories.summary: Kellogg School of Management has added seven new electives to its MBA programme. They run in the 2026-27 academic year and include building AI-powered solutions for real companies and field-based experiences. Course selection season just got longer.

stories.title: Northeastern launches an accelerated STEM-designated AI MBA
stories.summary: Northeastern's D'Amore-McKim School of Business is offering an accelerated, STEM-designated MBA focused on AI. The school says it builds analytical, technological and leadership capabilities for early-career professionals. The degree now comes with a shorter runway.

stories.title: Demand rises for MBAs in sustainable business
stories.summary: Demand for MBAs in sustainable business is rising in India, with IIM Lucknow, XIM and TERI SAS among the schools named. Reported packages range from ₹12 to over 30 LPA. Sustainability is now a career track with placement statistics.

stories.title: UK graduate visa returns to two years at high-compliance universities
stories.summary: The UK will extend the graduate visa from 18 months to two years for students at high-compliance universities, and widen the High Potential Individual route to graduates of the top 150 institutions. Applicants will be checking rankings closely.

stories.title: Sweden plans a global jobs website and wants Indian students to apply directly
stories.summary: Sweden plans to launch a website listing available jobs, open to applicants worldwide, says ambassador Petra Menander. Her priority is getting Indian students to apply directly to Swedish institutions, and Sweden does not expect its universities to open campuses in India. Winter coats not included.

stories.title: Anthropic's Felix Rieseberg says he stopped running coding interviews
stories.summary: In a blog post on 27 October, Anthropic engineering manager Felix Rieseberg wrote that he has stopped asking candidates to take coding interviews because Claude is now better at them. He argues newcomers bring fresh eyes. Candidates will need another reason to rehearse on a whiteboard.

stories.title: Accenture HR lead says companies will redesign operating models around AI
stories.summary: Iuliana Horsia, HR Partner Lead at Accenture, says organisations will redesign their operating models around AI. Speaking in Bucharest, she said companies have so far focused on tools, training and agents, and the next stage needs a rethink of how they operate. The org chart awaits.

stories.title: Average increments of 9% are being absorbed by city living costs
stories.summary: Indian companies are offering average annual increments of about 9%, but food, housing, transport, loans and insurance are absorbing much of the rise before it reaches savings. The pressure is sharpest in cities. The appraisal letter and the rent letter arrive in the same month.

stories.title: KPMG in Malta launches a free Accounts A Level tuition scholarship
stories.summary: KPMG in Malta has launched a scholarship offering free tuition for Accounts at A Level. The firm is starting its recruitment pipeline earlier than most. Debits and credits now come before driving lessons.

stories.title: Princeton Review ranks Binghamton best in SUNY for value and career placement
stories.summary: The Princeton Review has ranked Binghamton University best in the SUNY system for value and career placement, and 19th among best value public institutions. Admissions brochures are already being updated.

events.line: PAHO webinar on information systems for health workforce planning, with English interpretation.

research.title: What is Work For? Labor, Politics, and Meaning in the Age of AI
research.summary: Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper investigates the role of work in providing meaning, purpose, community, and other non-monetary benefits. Using an original cross-national survey of 8,234 working-age adults across the UK, US, Denmark, and India, I study the factors. Preprint, not peer reviewed.

research.title: A Proof for Generalized Egalitarianism
research.summary: Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper proves a rigidity theorem characterizing the Gini-type Lorenz-area ordering under general decision-theoretic constraints together with weak Lorenz dominance, thereby resolving the characterization problem pursued in this line of research on egalitarianism. This does not. Preprint, not peer reviewed.

research.title: Can Artificial Intelligence Forecast Treatment Effects in Economics?
research.summary: Announce Type: new Abstract: I use LLMs to forecast treatment effects of research studies pre-registered on the AEA RCT Registry and the Open Science Framework. I focus on studies whose results were first publicly released in 2026 and elicit forecasts. Preprint, not peer reviewed.

research.title: Capital growth since the 19th century
research.summary: Announce Type: new Abstract: We argued in an earlier paper (Getty and Tkachenko 2025b), from data reported for net saving and market-value capital by 94 nations over the period 1980-2021, that net saving has had little or no effect on. Preprint, not peer reviewed.

research.title: Crowds Believe in You: Online Prediction Markets Overestimate How Often People Achieve Their Own Goals
research.summary: Announce Type: cross Abstract: People increasingly share personal goals online and invite others to forecast them. Research on the planning fallacy finds that observers predict a person's behavior less optimistically than the person does, and prediction markets aggregate such judgments. Preprint, not peer reviewed.

research.title: Did the energy crisis turn borrowers green? Zonal power prices and green bond choice on Oslo B{\o}rs
research.summary: Announce Type: new Abstract: The energy crisis of 2021 to 2023 caused a sharp increase in Nordic electricity prices, with substantial differences across bidding zones. We use this variation to examine whether issuers exposed to higher local electricity prices were. Preprint, not peer reviewed.

research.title: How Firms Export: An Assignment Theory of Export Organization
research.summary: Announce Type: replace Abstract: This paper develops a model in which direct exporters, indirect exporters, pure intermediaries, and hybrid exporters emerge endogenously from the assignment of products to export platforms. Firms differ in manufacturing and commercial capabilities. Manufacturing capability determines. Preprint, not peer reviewed.

research.title: Learning to Detect Recessions from Pseudo-out-of-sample Tests
research.summary: Announce Type: replace Abstract: Everyone is keen to know when a recession has started, but official announcements come only after several months, and real-time detection methods typically struggle---as the Great Recession showed. These methods face two challenges. First, they rely. Preprint, not peer reviewed.
